description.p: Omatrack is a native telemetry workstation for drivers and engineers. It normalizes heterogeneous logger formats into one lap model for trace overlays, distance-aligned delta, corner analysis, and synchronized onboard video.

ul.li: Reads Pi/Cosworth PDS, MoTeC LD, Racelogic VBO, and AiM MP4 telemetry
Compares laps with or without usable GPS
Keeps source telemetry and video immutable

description.p: Measured Track Atlas maps show current and reference GPS lines, synchronized cursor markers, and automatic corner detail with reliable sub-metre GPS. Cached maps remain available offline.
A compact library sidebar, docked video opening, continuous playback, pit-stop filmstrip cells, and improved reference sync make it easier to explore and compare recorded laps.
Custom trace layouts add exact heights, manual scrolling, shared lanes, and independent styling. Corner editing stays responsive, and closing corner analysis reliably restores the previous viewport.
Windows fullscreen video stays a composited window: no display re-mode or refresh-rate switch, no black flicker, and dialogs can appear above the video.
Gauge discovery is opt-in per video and builds confidence by vote: boxes appear only after independent frames agree, larger gauges win over the glyph boxes nested in them, and boxes never overlap.
Discover, confirm and extract gauges from video with the offline model bundle: proven reader, tiny general detector and the larger AiM detector, all verified and shipped without downloads.

Progressive image-derived telemetry for supported video overlays, resumable telemetry caches, native time traces, optional Hugging Face model download and updates, and fullscreen video opening. Native telemetry remains authoritative and source footage stays local.

In-app updates from GitHub Releases for the Linux AppImage, Windows Velopack installer, and macOS app. Later snoozes the prompt for a week; the header icon stays. Windows installs per-user and asks about file associations on first run.

Native .telemetry companions as the only analysis file, primary video as the playback clock with reference catch-up on straights, five fullscreen compose layouts, an iRacing-style live delta bar, and Δt taken at the same 50 Hz lap-progress station as traces and video. Sidebar rows group by day. Corner notes and hover chips use that same station map.

S3 and Google Cloud Storage library sources, streamed onboard video with offline pin and signed-URL recovery, portable recording sidecars and create-only AiM companions, automatic USB discovery, representative lap selection, and non-blocking library I/O.

Session-confidence trace bands, multi-lap brake-point consistency, improved corner focus guides, stabilized dual-video synchronization, click-only video seeking from traces, and a compact fixed-position fullscreen telemetry HUD.

GPU scene-graph trace renderer, in-place corner analysis with a pluggable check system, authenticated WebDAV telemetry sources, Windows flat release zips, and unified telemetry/video file opening with recent-file history.

Cached GPS/speed track-station alignment shared by traces, delta and synchronized video; lazy cached library indexing; pinned upstream Rust telemetry crates; fullscreen telemetry HUD and video/folder metadata workflow; downloadable Linux, macOS and Windows builds.
